question: The chart below shows the total number of minutes (in billions) of telephone calls in the UK, divided into three categories, from 1995-2002. Summarise the information by selecting a reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
essay:
The bar chart illustrates the total duration, measured in billions of minutes, of telephone calls made in the United Kingdom across three categories between 1995 and 2002.

Overall, local fixed line calls were the most popular type throughout the entire period, although their share declined after 1999. In contrast, mobile calls grew steadily and consistently over the eight years.

In 1995, local fixed line calls accounted for approximately 72 billion minutes, which was considerably higher than national and international fixed line calls at around 38 billion minutes. Mobile calls were negligible at that point, standing at roughly 2 billion minutes.

Local fixed line usage rose to a peak of about 90 billion minutes in 1999, before falling back to approximately 72 billion minutes by 2002. Meanwhile, national and international calls increased gradually and reached around 61 billion minutes in the final year.

Mobile calls, despite starting from the lowest position, experienced the most dramatic growth, rising to about 46 billion minutes by 2002, a more than twentyfold increase.
